title: Episode 137: 🇬🇧 Sean Parent on Val (vs Rust)!

sentences.en: So we think there's an opportunity and a need for another language that's more approachable
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为，还有机会也需要一种比 Rust 更平易近人的语言，

sentences.en: than Rust, more safety than Carbon or CPP2 or anything that C++ could do in the next decade.
sentences.zh: 比 Carbon、CPP2 或 C++ 在未来十年内能做的任何事情都更安全。

sentences.en: You've got the creator of Rust saying that it's the language that he wished he created.
sentences.zh: 连 Rust 的创造者都说，这是他希望自己能创造出来的语言。

sentences.en: I'll ask him more directly.
sentences.zh: 我会更直接地问他。

sentences.en: Are you building a Rust competitor?
sentences.zh: 你在打造一个 Rust 的竞争对手吗？

sentences.en: I mean, Dave Abrahams and I decided just this last week that we're going to stop referring to VAL as an experimental language.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Dave Abrahams 和我上周刚决定，我们将不再把 VAL 称为实验性语言。

sentences.en: You heard it here first, folks.
sentences.zh: 各位，你们在这里先听到了。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 137, recorded on June 29th, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 137 期，录制于 2023 年 6 月 29 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we catch up with Sean Parent live from C++ on C2023.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，在 C++ on C2023 现场采访了 Sean Parent。

sentences.en: We chat about the VAL programming language and how it compares to programming languages like Rust, Swift, and C++.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了聊 VAL 编程语言，以及它与 Rust、Swift 和 C++ 等编程语言的对比。

sentences.zh: 关于斯洛文尼亚就到此为止，因为我们有件大事要宣布，各位。

sentences.en: Oh, wait, our wires are, it is the return of the king.
sentences.zh: 哦，等等，我们的线……是王者归来了。

sentences.zh: 等等，我们要查一下上次吗？Sean，你知道我们上次邀请你是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Episode one, something like that.
sentences.zh: 第一期，大概是那样。

sentences.en: We're bad friends, Sean.
sentences.zh: 我们真是糟糕的朋友，Sean。

sentences.en: It's like every, every, like, ten episodes, we're like, oh, yeah, we've got to have Sean back on.
sentences.zh: 就像每隔十期，我们就会说，哦，对了，我们得把 Sean 请回来。

sentences.en: But we're too, like, you guys are just completely trolling me.
sentences.zh: 但我们太……你们完全是在逗我玩。

sentences.en: I'm like, like, you keep saying you're going to ask to have me on, but then you don't actually ask to have me on.
sentences.zh: 我心想，你们一直说要邀请我，但实际上并没有真的邀请。

sentences.en: See, just don't mistake incompetence for malice.
sentences.zh: 看，别把无能当成恶意。

sentences.en: Solely incompetence.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是无能。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So, how have you been doing?
sentences.zh: 那么，你最近怎么样？

sentences.en: I've been doing well.
sentences.zh: 我过得不错。

sentences.en: So, since last time we talked, I think I started Software Technology Lab.
sentences.zh: 自从上次交谈以来，我想我创办了软件技术实验室（Software Technology Lab）。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, which is huge.
sentences.zh: 是的，这可是件大事。

sentences.en: What is the Software Technology Lab?
sentences.zh: 什么是软件技术实验室？

sentences.en: So, it's a group at Adobe, which is currently myself, David Abrahams, David Senkel, and Nick DeMarco, which is my small dream team.
sentences.zh: 它是 Adobe 的一个小组，目前成员包括我、David Abrahams、David Senkel 和 Nick DeMarco，这是我的梦之队。

sentences.en: Yes, I was just about to say, what a dream team.
sentences.zh: 是的，我正想说，真是个梦之队。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, our charter is improving software engineering practice, full stop, which I'll explain in a moment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的宗旨是改进软件工程实践，句号，我稍后会解释。

sentences.en: We define that as being distinct from process, which means we're not concerned with agile or other methods of software development.
sentences.zh: 我们将它定义为与流程截然不同，这意味着我们不关心敏捷或其他软件开发方法。

sentences.en: We're concerned with how do engineers write correct and efficient code when they sit down at the keyboard, and how do we make that happen.
sentences.zh: 我们关心的是工程师在坐在键盘前时，如何编写正确且高效的代码，以及我们如何实现这一点。

sentences.en: So, we're taking a three-pronged approach or three-pillar approach, which is education.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们采取三管齐下的方法，或者说三根支柱的方法，第一是教育。

sentences.en: So, we have a series right now, they're internal seminars, but they will become external seminars, and we kind of polish them up.
sentences.zh: 我们目前有一系列内部研讨会，但我们会把它们打磨好，变成外部研讨会。

sentences.en: Somewhat based on my Better Code series of talks, we're all working on the book, which is part of our educational emphasis.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上基于我的“更好的代码”（Better Code）系列讲座，我们都在写书，这也是我们教育重点的一部分。

sentences.en: It can be pre-ordered on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 它可以在亚马逊上预订。

sentences.en: It can be, but don't, because it doesn't ship until I retire.
sentences.zh: 是可以预订，但别买，因为在我退休之前它不会发货。

sentences.en: Connor, have you pre-ordered the book?
sentences.zh: Connor，你预订这本书了吗？

sentences.en: I may have pre-ordered it a couple years ago.
sentences.zh: 我可能几年前就预订了。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't tell my publisher.
sentences.zh: 嘿，别告诉我出版商。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So, yeah, but we're making progress.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们正在取得进展。

sentences.en: More progress than I was making alone, that's for sure.
sentences.zh: 比我一个人单打独斗进展快多了，那是肯定的。

sentences.en: Our next pillar is tooling.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二个支柱是工具。

sentences.en: So, we're renewing our effort in the STLab libraries, which are out there in open source, as well as the ASL libraries.
sentences.zh: 我们正在加大对 STLab 库的投入，这些库已经在开源了，还有 ASL 库。

sentences.en: And we're working on a language called Val.
sentences.zh: 我们还在开发一种叫 Val 的语言。

sentences.en: And then our third pillar is research, which includes university collaboration.
sentences.zh: 第三个支柱是研究，包括与大学的合作。

sentences.en: I've got an ongoing collaboration with Yaku Yarve, but we're looking for other universities to kind of restart our efforts in this area.
sentences.zh: 我与 Yaku Yarve 有持续的合作，但我们正在寻找其他大学，以重启我们在这一领域的努力。

sentences.en: And back to the full stop, the original charter of the team, or the old software technology lab,
sentences.zh: 回到刚才说的“句号”，该团队最初的章程，或者说旧的软件技术实验室，

sentences.en: which I managed before with Alex Stepanoff and Paul McTones and Matt Marcus and Foster Brereton.
sentences.zh: 我之前和 Alex Stepanoff、Paul McTones、Matt Marcus 以及 Foster Brereton 一起管理过。

sentences.en: Our charter then was much the same.
sentences.zh: 我们当时的章程也差不多。

sentences.en: It was improved software engineering practice at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 就是改进 Adobe 的软件工程实践。

sentences.en: And this time around, we had a VP with enough insight to say it should not be at Adobe.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，我们有一位副总裁，他有足够的洞察力说，这不应该局限于 Adobe。

sentences.en: It should be industry-wide, so do this publicly and visible.
sentences.zh: 它应该是全行业范围的，所以要公开且透明地做。

sentences.en: So, we are all going to get to benefit from the great content that Mr. Sean Perrin and his dream team are going to put out.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所有人都能从 Sean Perrin 先生和他的梦之队将要发布的内容中受益。

sentences.en: That is our goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的目标。

sentences.en: That is our goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的目标。

sentences.en: Speaking of Val, we were having dinner on Tuesday night, and I did not know this, but you said that the creator, the original creator of Russ, Graydon Hoare,
sentences.zh: 说到 Val，周二晚上我们吃晚饭时，我不知道这件事，但你说 Rust 的原作者 Graydon Hoare，

sentences.en: had comments about the Val language that I did not know about.
sentences.zh: 对 Val 语言有一些评价，我之前不知道。

sentences.en: Share with our listeners what the original creator of Russ, Graydon Hoare, said about Val.
sentences.zh: 和我们的听众分享一下 Rust 的原作者 Graydon Hoare 对 Val 的评价吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so you can look at this up on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 好的，你们可以在 Twitter 上查到。

sentences.en: You can put it in your show notes.
sentences.zh: 你们可以把它放在节目笔记里。

sentences.en: So, Graydon posted on Twitter that Val is the language he wished he created.
sentences.zh: Graydon 在 Twitter 上发帖说，Val 是他希望自己能创造出来的语言。

sentences.en: Wow, what an endorsement.
sentences.zh: 哇，真是极高的赞誉。

sentences.en: So, what should we know about Val?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于 Val 我们应该知道些什么？

sentences.en: What is, you know, my colleague Andre, our colleague Andre, you know, likes to say that a language has to be 10x better than the competitors on some axis to really survive.
sentences.zh: 我的同事 Andre，我们的同事 Andre，常说一种语言必须在某个维度上比竞争对手好 10 倍才能真正生存下来。

sentences.en: What is the 10x for Val?
sentences.zh: Val 的 10 倍优势是什么？

sentences.en: What is our 10x?
sentences.zh: 我们的 10 倍优势是什么？

sentences.en: So, I think our 10x is pushing the idea of mutable value semantics, which is really the idea of regular types that Stepanov was promoting as part of the STL.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的 10 倍优势在于推动“可变值语义”（mutable value semantics）的理念，这实际上就是 Stepanov 在 STL 中推广的常规类型理念。

sentences.en: Pushing that as being the fundamental way that you describe objects and computation within the language.
sentences.zh: 将其作为描述语言中对象和计算的基本方式来推广。

sentences.en: Right now, what's happening, folks?
sentences.zh: 现在发生了什么，各位？

sentences.zh: Sean Barrett 刚刚把我的酒杯倒满了，可能比应该倒的量多了一倍。

sentences.en: So, Connor topped up his wine.
sentences.zh: 所以 Connor 把他的酒续上了。

sentences.en: And then Sean topped up the top up.
sentences.zh: 然后 Sean 又给续杯续上了。

sentences.zh: 这两个人已经准备就绪，蓄势待发了。

sentences.zh: 我们去找些椅子吧。

sentences.zh: 因为我觉得，你们两个待会儿得被人抬出去。

sentences.zh: 我们已经超时四分钟了。

sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实得离开这个房间。

sentences.zh: 我们还有 J.F. 在。

sentences.zh: 他戴着 Apple Watch，尽管我很喜欢那家公司。

sentences.zh: 他确实戴了。

sentences.zh: 不用让别人审批你的动画感觉如何？

sentences.en: Oh, it's great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.zh: 可以说原因吗？

sentences.zh: Twitter 上有。

sentences.zh: Twitter 上有。

sentences.zh: 我解释过了。

sentences.en: It's a fun fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的事实。

sentences.en: It's my most popular tweet.
sentences.zh: 这是我最受欢迎的推文。

sentences.en: My most popular tweet is how Apple would not let me use anvil drop.
sentences.zh: 我最受欢迎的推文就是关于苹果不让我用铁砧掉落动画的事。

sentences.en: So, yeah, good job, me.
sentences.zh: 所以，干得好，我。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: We're going to camp out right here.
sentences.zh: 我们要在这里驻扎下来。

sentences.en: Before we were so rudely interrupted, Sean was explaining what gives Val the 10x advantage.
sentences.zh: 在我们被粗暴打断之前，Sean 正在解释 Val 的 10 倍优势是什么。

sentences.en: So Val is centered around value semantics and basically how far can we push that paradigm.
sentences.zh: Val 是以值语义为核心的，基本上就是看我们能把这种范式推到什么程度。

sentences.en: But if you look, so Chris Ladner, who created LLVM, also started the Swift language.
sentences.zh: 如果你看的话，Chris Lattner，LLVM 的创造者，也创建了 Swift 语言。

sentences.en: And Dave Abrahams kind of left the C++ community to work on Swift and to do the Swift standard library.
sentences.zh: Dave Abrahams 离开了 C++ 社区去开发 Swift，并编写了 Swift 标准库。

sentences.en: And one of Dave's contribution there was bringing some of Alex Stepanov's ideas into Swift.
sentences.zh: Dave 在那里的贡献之一就是将 Alex Stepanov 的一些思想引入了 Swift。

sentences.en: And so if you look at Swift, it's a little bit of a bifurcated language.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看 Swift，它是一种稍微有些分叉的语言。

sentences.en: It's got a reference semantic portion, which is there for compatibility with Objective-C.
sentences.zh: 它有一部分引用语义，那是为了与 Objective-C 兼容。

sentences.en: But the entire standard library is written in terms of value semantics.
sentences.zh: 但整个标准库都是用值语义编写的。

sentences.en: And that's Dave Abraham's work.
sentences.zh: 那是 Dave Abrahams 的工作。

sentences.en: And Swift also takes the ideas of concepts and kind of the work that Jeremy Seek did.
sentences.zh: Swift 也采用了概念（concepts）的思想，以及 Jeremy Siek 所做的工作。

sentences.en: And then Doug Greger did for Concept C++, which was concepts pre-C++11, not the concepts we have in the current language for anybody who's too young to remember.
sentences.zh: 还有 Doug Gregor 为 Concept C++ 所做的工作，那是 C++11 之前的概念，不是当前语言里的概念，给那些太年轻不记得的人提个醒。

sentences.en: So Doug Greger took Jeremy Seek's ideas and incorporated those into RuSt.
sentences.zh: 所以 Doug Gregor 采纳了 Jeremy Siek 的思想并将其融入了 Rust。

sentences.en: And so arguably, Rust has kind of better concepts than C++ has.
sentences.zh: 可以说，Rust 的概念比 C++ 的更好。

sentences.en: I don't think there's much arguably there.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这有什么争议。

sentences.en: I think it's just a true fact.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个事实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Demi Recordon, who's a postdoc out of Northeastern, took the idea of kind of value semantic Swift and did her thesis work on basically how far could you push value semantics.
sentences.zh: 来自东北大学的博士后 Demi Recordon，采用了值语义 Swift 的思想，并以“能把值语义推到多远”为题完成了她的论文。

sentences.en: And could you make value semantics a first part of the language and make the language safe by default, even under a mutation?
sentences.zh: 你能不能让值语义成为语言的第一部分，并使语言在默认情况下是安全的，即使在可变的情况下？

sentences.en: And so you would have many of the benefits that you would have with Rust as far as worry-free concurrency.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能获得 Rust 在无忧并发方面的大部分好处。

sentences.en: You can't introduce a race condition because you can't have dual access to an object under mutation.
sentences.zh: 你无法引入竞态条件，因为你无法在可变状态下对同一个对象进行双重访问。

sentences.en: And those same ideas, but in a much simpler package.
sentences.zh: 这些思想是一样的，但封装得简单得多。

sentences.en: So if you think about, one way to think about Rust is Rust is a simpler form of pure functional programming.
sentences.zh: 如果你想一下，理解 Rust 的一种方式是，Rust 是纯函数式编程的一种简化形式。

sentences.en: Because in pure functional programming, you're always thinking about things in terms of mutation, but you can't actually express mutation.
sentences.zh: 因为在纯函数式编程中，你总是从可变性的角度思考问题，但你实际上无法表达可变性。

sentences.en: So you have to express mutation in terms of rewriting the universe to affect mutation.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须通过重写整个宇宙来影响可变性。

sentences.en: So in some sense, Rust is a simplified form of functional programming.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，Rust 是函数式编程的简化形式。

sentences.en: They're interchangeable, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，它们是可以互换的。

sentences.en: There's a fairly trivial transformation to go from Rust to FP.
sentences.zh: 从 Rust 到 FP 有一个相当简单的转换。

sentences.en: But Rust is an easier model to think about because now you can actually think in terms of mutation.
sentences.zh: 但 Rust 是一个更容易思考的模型，因为现在你真的可以从可变性的角度去思考了。

sentences.en: The problem is within Rust, you have to do that through annotations and a borrow checker.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在 Rust 中，你必须通过注解和借用检查器（borrow checker）来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And it becomes very complicated into how do you describe that you have right access to this object.
sentences.zh: 这变得非常复杂，比如你如何描述你对这个对象拥有写权限。

sentences.en: Whereas Val takes everything in terms of a whole-part relationship.
sentences.zh: 而 Val 将一切都视为整体与部分的关系。

sentences.en: And through the whole-part relationship, it can track, oh, if you have right access to the whole, then you have right access to the parts.
sentences.zh: 通过整体与部分的关系，它可以追踪到：哦，如果你对整体拥有写权限，那么你对部分也拥有写权限。

sentences.en: And if you have right access to the parts, then you can hand out right access to some of your parts to this process and some of your parts to that process.
sentences.zh: 如果你对部分拥有写权限，那么你可以将部分写权限分发给这个进程，将另一些部分写权限分发给那个进程。

sentences.en: And so you can get kind of the benefits of Rust
sentences.zh: 所以你可以获得 Rust 的好处，

sentences.en: without all of the decoration and all the complexity.
sentences.zh: 而无需所有的装饰和复杂性。

sentences.en: You start to think about things just in terms of a model that you have in most programming languages, which is your built-in types like your ints, if they're not boxed,
sentences.zh: 你开始从大多数编程语言中都有的模型来思考问题，即内置类型，比如 int，如果它们不是装箱的，

sentences.en: are these types that are just on your stack that you just use.
sentences.zh: 它们就是堆栈上你直接使用的类型。

sentences.en: And in Val, you can think about it as everything behaves like an int.
sentences.zh: 在 Val 中，你可以认为一切都像 int 一样运行。

sentences.en: But you have all the protection there to say, I can't create a race condition on my int.
sentences.zh: 但你拥有所有的保护措施，可以说，我无法在我的 int 上产生竞态条件。

sentences.en: But I have all the efficiencies as if I were handing out references, but they behave as if I were handing out values.
sentences.zh: 但我拥有所有高效的特性，就像我在分发引用一样，但它们的行为表现却像是分发值。

sentences.en: So within the Rust model, things like move is implicit.
sentences.zh: 所以在 Rust 模型中，像移动（move）这样的操作是隐式的。

sentences.en: So if I assign one thing to another thing, that's just a move.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我把一个东西赋值给另一个东西，那仅仅是一个移动操作。

sentences.en: And it's a destructive move.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个破坏性的移动。

sentences.en: I can't reference that object anymore.
sentences.zh: 我无法再引用那个对象了。

sentences.en: It has fallen out of scope.
sentences.zh: 它已经超出了作用域。

sentences.en: An object that's under mutation during an exception disappears.
sentences.zh: 一个在异常期间正在发生变异的对象会消失。

sentences.en: An object that I hand off to a thread is no longer in scope within my current scope.
sentences.zh: 一个我移交给线程的对象，在我当前的作用域内就不再存在了。

sentences.en: Well, at the same time that you have that whole environment going on, and you're doing that all without additional annotation and decoration, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在拥有整个环境的同时，你无需额外的注解和修饰就能做到这一切，对吧？

sentences.en: So it becomes, our argument is if you look at how people use Swift and how people use the Swift standard library,
sentences.zh: 所以我们的论点是，如果你看看人们如何使用 Swift 以及如何使用 Swift 标准库，

sentences.en: people view that as being a simpler model, and it's easier to program.
sentences.zh: 人们认为那是一个更简单的模型，编程起来更容易。

sentences.en: And it's very approachable, and you have like the Swift playground, and people jump into it very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常容易上手，你有像 Swift Playground 这样的工具，人们很快就能上手。

sentences.en: And so DIMI took that and basically put it on a strong theoretical foundation, proving its correctness, proving that it satisfies the frame rule,
sentences.zh: 所以 DIMI 采用了这一点，并基本上将其建立在坚实的理论基础之上，证明了它的正确性，证明了它满足框架规则（frame rule），

sentences.en: which I talked about in my previous talk, which means it satisfies the non-interference pattern, which means it, or non-interference property,
sentences.zh: 我在之前的演讲中谈到过这一点，这意味着它满足非干扰模式，或者说非干扰属性，

sentences.en: which means it's a system that has all the safeties, all the memory safety, all the security.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它是一个具备所有安全性、内存安全性和保障性的系统。

sentences.en: All the concurrency that you would want, but in a much more efficient way than you would get in a language with no mutability like Haskell.
sentences.zh: 它具备你想要的所有并发性，但比像 Haskell 这种没有可变性的语言要高效得多。

sentences.en: Could you just, could you give the definition of that non-interference principle that you gave in the talk?
sentences.zh: 你能否给出你在演讲中提到的那个非干扰原则的定义？

sentences.en: Because I think that may be helpful for...
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这可能会有帮助……

sentences.en: Yeah, so the non-interference property is basically that an operation can only affect objects that are passed directly in its interface and can't affect other objects.
sentences.zh: 好的，非干扰属性基本上是指一个操作只能影响直接通过其接口传递的对象，而不能影响其他对象。

sentences.en: So this relates to the whole part relationship.
sentences.zh: 这与整体与部分的关系有关。

sentences.en: If I pass something to, you know, through my interface, I can only affect those things in the interface.
sentences.zh: 如果我通过接口传递了某个东西，我只能影响接口中的那些东西。

sentences.en: I can't affect other objects.
sentences.zh: 我无法影响其他对象。

sentences.en: In a reference semantic language like JavaScript or Python or something like that, that reference is shared.
sentences.zh: 在像 JavaScript 或 Python 这样的引用语义语言中，引用是共享的。

sentences.en: And so if I access the object through my interface,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我通过我的接口访问该对象，

sentences.en: I'm also touching the object potentially that somebody else has access to, that the objects intersect.
sentences.zh: 我也可能触及其他人可以访问的对象，即这些对象存在交集。

sentences.en: And so Val does not allow that intersection.
sentences.zh: 而 Val 不允许这种交集。

sentences.en: So it doesn't allow that level of interference.
sentences.zh: 所以它不允许那种程度的干扰。

sentences.en: Rust doesn't allow that level of interference either.
sentences.zh: Rust 也不允许那种程度的干扰。

sentences.en: It's just more complicated to get to.
sentences.zh: 只是实现起来更复杂一些。

sentences.en: But does this mean that...
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着……

sentences.en: Doesn't this mean that you have some restrictions?
sentences.zh: 这难道不意味着你有一些限制吗？

sentences.en: Like, how would you write a linked list in Val?
sentences.zh: 比如，你如何在 Val 中编写链表？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it has many of the restrictions as Rust there, which means that in order to implement a linked list, for anybody who doesn't know, the problem with a linked list
sentences.zh: 是的，它在那里有许多和 Rust 一样的限制，这意味着为了实现链表，对于任何不知道的人来说，链表的问题在于

sentences.en: is you're trying to refer both frontwards and backwards,
sentences.zh: 你试图同时向前和向后引用，

sentences.en: you know, in a doubly linked list within your cells, which means you require mutable access to both and it has to be shared between both.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在双向链表的单元格内，这意味着你需要对两者进行可变访问，并且它必须在两者之间共享。

sentences.en: Val allows you to step out into an unsafe construct and then build safe mechanisms on top of that.
sentences.zh: Val 允许你进入不安全结构，然后在上面构建安全机制。

sentences.en: So we can build that with unsafe constructs and then put a safe API around that in the same way that Rust can pull those things off.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以用不安全结构来构建它，然后在其周围加上一个安全的 API，就像 Rust 实现这些功能的方式一样。

sentences.en: Right now within Val, unsafe is only at the statement level.
sentences.zh: 目前在 Val 中，不安全（unsafe）仅限于语句级别。

sentences.en: We don't have block unsafe, which Rust does.
sentences.zh: 我们没有像 Rust 那样的不安全代码块。

sentences.en: And that's because we actually think the need for unsafe is less than it is in RuSt.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们认为对不安全的需求比在 Rust 中要少。

sentences.en: And part of that is Rust mutability is to an entire heap-allocated object, right?
sentences.zh: 部分原因是 Rust 的可变性是针对整个堆分配对象的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's still a reference semantic language.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是一种引用语义语言。

sentences.en: You have heap-allocated objects.
sentences.zh: 你有堆分配的对象。

sentences.en: You want access to that object.
sentences.zh: 你想要访问那个对象。

sentences.en: You need access to all of it, all of its parts, everything.
sentences.zh: 你需要访问它的全部，它的所有部分，所有东西。

sentences.en: Within Val, we're not dealing with reference semantics.
sentences.zh: 在 Val 中，我们处理的不是引用语义。

sentences.en: We're dealing with value semantics.
sentences.zh: 我们处理的是值语义。

sentences.en: And that means if you have right access to the object as a whole,
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你拥有对整个对象的写访问权限，

sentences.en: you can slice that up.
sentences.zh: 你可以将其切片。

sentences.en: And you can say, oh, I want to grant right access to just these parts over here and just these parts over here.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，哦，我只想授予这部分和那部分的写访问权限。

sentences.en: So the need for doing unsafe code is greatly reduced because you don't have to say, oh, I need to grant right access
sentences.zh: 所以编写不安全代码的需求大大减少了，因为你不必说，哦，我需要授予

sentences.en: to these two things so that they can coordinate between these parts.
sentences.zh: 这两样东西写访问权限，以便它们可以在这些部分之间进行协调。

sentences.en: You can say, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I can grant right access to this portion for this piece of code and so they're just parts of the same object.
sentences.zh: 我可以为这段代码授予这部分的写访问权限，所以它们只是同一个对象的不同部分。

sentences.en: So you can think about it within a vector just because I can pass off mutability access to the first element of the vector without passing off mutability to the vector as a whole.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把它想象成一个向量，仅仅因为我可以移交向量第一个元素的可变访问权限，而无需移交整个向量的可变性。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: That makes a lot of sense, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这非常有道理，是的。

sentences.en: I've got a quick question here.
sentences.zh: 我这里有个简短的问题。

sentences.en: So back at CPP North 2022, when you gave your keynote of, I think it was C++, A Tragedy in Two Parts, which was got to be one of the best talks that I've seen from you.
sentences.zh: 回到 CPP North 2022，当你发表主题演讲时，我想是《C++，两部分的悲剧》，那一定是我看过你最好的演讲之一。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got so many good talks.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你有很多精彩的演讲。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was one of my favorite Sean talks.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是 Sean 最让我喜欢的演讲之一。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll link in the description all of his best talks, obviously C++ seasoning.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们会在描述中链接他所有最好的演讲，显然还有《C++ Seasoning》。

sentences.en: My favorite still is that keynote at C++ Now.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的仍然是 C++ Now 上的那个主题演讲。

sentences.en: A vignette in three parts?
sentences.zh: 《三部分的短片》？

sentences.en: Yes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So I was about to, like, before Bryce interrupted, I was about to say that one because I feel like, honestly,
sentences.zh: 我刚才，在 Bryce 打断我之前，正想说那个，因为我觉得说实话，

sentences.en: A Vignette in Three Parts was, like, eight years prior to you giving this talk, kind of like you echoed the same things of, like, how GPUs are underutilized and how that's the...
sentences.zh: 《三部分的短片》是在你做这次演讲的八年前，你当时就呼应了同样的事情，比如 GPU 是如何被低估的，以及那才是……

sentences.en: Anyways, we'll link all of Sean's greatest hits in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们会在节目笔记中链接 Sean 的所有代表作。

sentences.en: But in that talk, you mentioned Val, and you mentioned Val as kind of just, like, a research language that didn't have any large goals of, like, superseding any other languages.
sentences.zh: 但在那次演讲中，你提到了 Val，你提到 Val 只是作为一种研究语言，没有任何想要取代其他任何语言的宏大目标。

sentences.en: And if the greatest impact that it had was influencing C++ into a better direction, that that would be, like, a successful goal.
sentences.zh: 如果它产生的最大影响是引导 C++ 走向更好的方向，那将是一个成功的目标。

sentences.en: But now you've got the creator of Rust saying that it's the language that he wished he created.
sentences.zh: 但现在 Rust 的创造者说这是他希望自己创造的语言。

sentences.en: I'm listening to you and Bryce chat, and you're saying that the need for unsafe is a lot less, and you don't even have unsafe blocks.
sentences.zh: 我听着你和 Bryce 聊天，你说对不安全的需求少了很多，甚至没有不安全代码块。

sentences.en: You only have unsafe at the statement level.
sentences.zh: 你只有语句级别的不安全。

sentences.en: So my question now is, I think we're about 11 months or 10 months since your keynote at that conference.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在的问题是，我想距离你在那次会议上的主题演讲已经过去 11 个月或 10 个月了。

sentences.en: Have the goals of Val changed, or is it still the same, and there's just, like, a lot of upside?
sentences.zh: Val 的目标改变了吗，还是依然如故，只是有很多潜在的优势？

sentences.en: I'll hand it over to Bryce.
sentences.zh: 我交给 Bryce 来回答。

sentences.en: I'll ask him more directly.
sentences.zh: 我会更直接地问他。

sentences.en: Are you building a Rust competitor?
sentences.zh: 你们是在构建一个 Rust 的竞争对手吗？

sentences.en: So, not quite yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还不完全是。

sentences.en: I mean, Dave Abrahams and I decided just this last week that we're going to stop referring to Val as an experimental language.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Dave Abrahams 和我上周刚决定，我们将不再把 Val 称为实验性语言。

sentences.en: You heard it here first, folks.
sentences.zh: 各位，你们在这里先听到了。

sentences.en: In part because we think the hypothesis we wanted to vet is,
sentences.zh: 部分原因是我们认为我们想要验证的假设是，

sentences.en: can you write significant applications in this kind of pure value semantic world?
sentences.zh: 你能在这种纯值语义的世界中编写重要的应用程序吗？

sentences.en: And we actually think that that question has been answered at this point by Swift.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上认为这个问题目前已经被 Swift 回答了。

sentences.en: So, like I said, Swift is kind of this bifurcated language.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像我说的，Swift 是一种分叉的语言。

sentences.en: It has many of the properties of Val.
sentences.zh: 它拥有 Val 的许多特性。

sentences.en: For people who don't know, if you declare a struct in Swift, it's kind of copy on write.
sentences.zh: 对于不知道的人，如果你在 Swift 中声明一个结构体，它有点像写时复制（copy on write）。

sentences.en: It has value semantics.
sentences.zh: 它具有值语义。

sentences.en: It doesn't quite have all the guarantees that Val has, but it's close.
sentences.zh: 它并不完全具备 Val 的所有保证，但已经很接近了。

sentences.en: And so we actually think that that hypothesis and that model is proven out at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上认为那个假设和模型在这一点上已经得到了证明。

sentences.en: The other thing that's happened is we've gotten to the point where we have an LLVM backend at this point that's functioning for Val.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，我们已经到了拥有一个 LLVM 后端的阶段，该后端目前可以为 Val 工作。

sentences.en: Dave Abrahams is busy working on the Val standard library, and so that's coming along.
sentences.zh: Dave Abrahams 正忙于编写 Val 标准库，所以进展顺利。

sentences.en: We're hoping to get Val available on GitHub.
sentences.zh: 我们希望让 Val 在 GitHub 上可用。

sentences.en: I was just talking with Matt Godbolt at this conference about the process for that.
sentences.zh: 我刚才在这次会议上和 Matt Godbolt 谈过这个过程。

sentences.en: But we think we have enough in place that we can actually make that happen.
sentences.zh: 但我们认为我们已经准备得足够充分，可以实现这一点。

sentences.en: But you said GitHub.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才说了 GitHub。

sentences.en: Did you mean Compiler Explorer?
sentences.zh: 你是说 Compiler Explorer 吗？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Compiler Explorer, yeah.
sentences.zh: Compiler Explorer，是的。

sentences.en: So we want Val is available on GitHub, but we want to make Val available on Compiler Explorer so people can start playing with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望 Val 在 GitHub 上可用，但我们想让 Val 在 Compiler Explorer 上可用，这样人们就可以开始尝试它了。

sentences.en: The other thing that's happened in that time frame, which is what my talk was about here, is that safety has become a much more significant issue,
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里发生的另一件事，也就是我在这里演讲的主题，是安全性已经成为一个更重要的问题，

sentences.en: and that's partially around legislation and what's going on in that domain.
sentences.zh: 这部分与立法以及该领域正在发生的事情有关。

sentences.en: And so we're looking at the industry is going to have to make, in our opinion, a fairly significant shift, at least sections of the industry,
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为行业将不得不做出一个相当重大的转变，至少是行业的部分领域，

sentences.en: towards more memory-safe languages.
sentences.zh: 转向更内存安全的语言。

sentences.en: And the only language out there right now that's commercially viable that meets the requirements that the security industry actually wants is RuSt.
sentences.zh: 目前市面上唯一商业可行且满足安全行业实际要求的语言是 Rust。

sentences.en: And we think Val has, you know, and if you talk to C++ developers who have tried to learn Rust, it's a little hit and miss.
sentences.zh: 我们认为 Val 有，你知道，如果你和尝试学习 Rust 的 C++ 开发人员交谈，效果有点参差不齐。

sentences.en: It's certainly better than, the uptake is better than C++ developers who have tried to learn Haskell,
sentences.zh: 当然，它的普及程度比尝试学习 Haskell 的 C++ 开发人员要好，

sentences.en: but learning Rust is still a bit of a mind warp for your typical developer.
sentences.zh: 但学习 Rust 对典型的开发人员来说仍然有点烧脑。

sentences.en: And a big part of that is just reasoning about lifetime and ownership is a problem, where we think if you say, everything behaves just like an int.
sentences.zh: 很大一部分原因是关于生命周期和所有权的推理是一个问题，而我们认为如果你说，一切表现得就像一个整数。

sentences.en: All of your classes are just like built-in types.
sentences.zh: 你所有的类都像内置类型一样。

sentences.en: And so like all the things you know about an int and the thread safety of an int and all of that, that just works.
sentences.zh: 所以就像你所知道的关于整数的所有事情，以及整数的线程安全性等等，这些都能直接工作。

sentences.en: We think that that's a much more approachable model and we think that Swift has proven that that's a much more approachable model.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是一个更容易上手的模型，我们认为 Swift 已经证明了这是一个更容易上手的模型。

sentences.en: And so Apple,
sentences.zh: 所以苹果，

sentences.en: if you were at C++ Now,
sentences.zh: 如果你在 C++ Now 的话，

sentences.en: John McCall, who's one of the creators of Swift, was at C++ Now.
sentences.zh: Swift 的创造者之一 John McCall 也在 C++ Now。

sentences.en: And he was talking about, you know,
sentences.zh: 他在谈论，你知道，

sentences.en: Apple in response to the legislation that's pending around memory safety and around security is looking to move critical subsystems of Apple's OS into Swift
sentences.zh: 苹果为了响应围绕内存安全和安全的立法，正在寻求将苹果操作系统的关键子系统迁移到 Swift，

sentences.en: and specifically into the value semantic area of Swift.
sentences.zh: 特别是迁移到 Swift 的值语义领域。

sentences.en: And Apple has some issues with perception around Swift, which is they're trying to make Swift open source and publicly available, but every time kind of push comes to shove,
sentences.zh: 苹果在 Swift 的认知方面存在一些问题，那就是他们试图让 Swift 开源并公开可用，但每当关键时刻，

sentences.en: the priorities are around what's Apple's next product,
sentences.zh: 优先级总是围绕着苹果的下一个产品，

sentences.en: not around the community around Swift.
sentences.zh: 而不是围绕 Swift 的社区。

sentences.en: And so if you look, this is why, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看，这就是为什么，你知道，

sentences.en: Chris Lattner left Apple to go to Google to create Swift for TensorFlow
sentences.zh: Chris Lattner 离开苹果去谷歌创建 Swift for TensorFlow。

sentences.en: at Google.
sentences.zh: 那并没有发生，因为苹果对 Swift 的控制太紧了。

sentences.en: That didn't happen because Apple kept the reins too tight
sentences.zh: 那并没有发生，因为苹果对 Swift 的控制太紧了。

sentences.en: on Swift.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为存在一个机会和需求，需要另一种比 Rust 更容易上手、比 Carbon 或 CPP2 或 C++ 在未来十年内能做的任何事情都更安全的语言。

sentences.en: And so we think there's an opportunity and a need for another language that's more approachable than Rust, more safety than Carbon or CPP2 or anything that C++ could do
sentences.zh: 所以存在一个缺口。

sentences.en: in the next decade.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望填补这个缺口。

sentences.en: So there's a gap.
sentences.zh: 你有没有

sentences.en: So we're hoping to fill that.
sentences.zh: 你以前构建过编程语言吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever
sentences.zh: 我构建过小型编程语言。

sentences.en: have you ever built a programming language before?
sentences.zh: 所以我从事过名为属性模型（property models）的工作，围绕它的语言叫 Atom，还有一个叫 Eve 的布局系统，这些在 Adobe 内部有大量使用。

sentences.en: I have built small programming languages.
sentences.zh: 在 Adobe 之外使用得不多。

sentences.en: So I've worked on on things called property models and the language around that is called Atom and a layout system called Eve and those have heavy use inside of Adobe.
sentences.zh: 它们是非常有趣的系统。

sentences.en: Not so heavy use outside of Adobe.
sentences.zh: 它们都编译成字节码，所以它们是解释型系统，而不是编译型系统。

sentences.en: They're very interesting systeMs.
sentences.zh: Dave Abrahams 是我们团队中唯一参与过几种不同成功语言的创建和演进的人。

sentences.en: They both compile to bytecode so they're interpreted systems and not compiled systeMs.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dave Abrahams is the one person on our team who has been involved in the creation and evolution of a few different successful languages.
